## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- US Census Bureau ACS 5-year API (via `tidycensus`): 2012–2016 ACS at the
  **tract** level and 2020–2024 ACS at both **tract** and **block-group** levels,
  California.
- `../../../data-raw-temp/nhgis/nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06/nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06.csv`
  — NHGIS geographic crosswalk, 2020 block groups → 2010 tracts (allocation weights).
- `../../../data-raw-temp/nhgis/nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06/nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06.csv`
  — NHGIS geographic crosswalk, 2000 tracts → 2010 tracts (allocation weights).

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step1_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS estimates, one row per 2010 CA tract.
- `../../../data/acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates, one row per 2020 CA block group.
- `../../../data/acs_step1_2024_tract.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates, one row per 2020 CA tract, consumed by the separate Step 2 tract-source path.
- `../../../data/xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather` — 2020 block group → 2010 tract crosswalk (weights).
- `../../../data/xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather` — 2000 tract → 2010 tract crosswalk (weights).

This notebook:

1. Set up environment (packages, block-group exclusions, helper functions, data paths)
2. Define target ACS variables
3. Import and prepare 2012–2016 ACS tract data
4. Import and prepare 2020–2024 ACS block-group data
5. Import and prepare 2020–2024 ACS tract data
6. Import and prepare geographic crosswalks
7. Validate outputs (including exact block-group/crosswalk readback)

Both tract downloads share `tract_vars` (65 aliases / 62 distinct Census codes).
The block-group list (62 aliases / 59 codes) excludes `rent1bdr`, `rent2bdr`, and
`rent3bdr`, configured explicitly in §1.2 because these B25031 variables are
unavailable at block-group grain. B25111 and B25113 measures are removed from
both years; `vac_forrent` and `vac_rented` are retained in all three requests.

The retired low-rent counts are not constructed. All gross-rent bins remain
available for downstream interpolation.

For each extract, a separate B25064 E/EA/M/MA request preserves original
character codes in `rent_source_e`, `rent_source_ea`, `rent_source_m`, and
`rent_source_ma`, with logical `rent_evidence_available`. Match GEOIDs and
normalized E/M exactly before attaching evidence. If retrieval fails, preserve
normalized E/M, missing annotations, and availability FALSE for cautious
upstream classification. Dollar units remain the source-year basis; no bounds
or classifications are constructed here.

This step only **imports and stores** source data; it performs no row-level
filtering or sample restriction. Geographic harmonization (aggregating the
2020–2024 block-group data to 2010 tracts using these crosswalks) happens in
`02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd`. `02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd` retains native 2020
tracts and constructs the same direct tract measures as the 2016 path.
Generate the newly named inputs
from this notebook; old caches do not implement the revised variable contract.
Existing data files are retained. Stage 2 now adds rental inventory from the
three required estimates with explicit missingness propagation, using `wt_renthu`
for block-group components and direct sums for both tract sources. Its narrow
schema migration for the existing 2016 and block-group products permits
the agreed additions/removals against older parity references while retaining
strict checks on shared columns; see [README.md](README.md).

The block-group extract and allocation crosswalk pass structural assertions
before saving. Section 6.1 reports statewide ACS-only and crosswalk-only block
groups for analyst review; these coverage differences do not establish tract
completeness. Section 7.6 compares both saved inputs exactly with their validated
in-memory objects, including every allocation weight.

## 1.2 Variables unavailable at block-group grain

### Decision: Configure block-group exclusions explicitly

The three bedroom-rent measures below remain in both tract downloads and are
omitted from the 2024 block-group request and output. The installed geography
lookup lacks 2024 entries, so it must not automatically determine exclusions.
B25111 and B25113 are removed from the full list in §2.2 and are not exclusions.

```{r configure-block-group-exclusions}
block_group_unavailable_vars <- c(
  "rent1bdr",  # B25031_003
  "rent2bdr",  # B25031_004
  "rent3bdr"   # B25031_005
)
```

## 1.3 Load helper functions

Reusable helpers (`summ_var()`, `rename_id()`, `save_data()`,
and the diagnostic helpers `report_n()` / `print_numeric_summary()`) live in
`R/helpers.R` and are loaded here. Keeping them in one documented file lets every
notebook in this stage share the same definitions.
Step 1 input assertions, coverage diagnostics, and exact readback checks live
in `R/acs_input_qa.R`.

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "rent_metadata.R"))
source(here::here("R", "helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "acs_input_qa.R"))
```

## 1.4 Set data paths

All paths are relative to this repository, which is the integration point
between pipeline stages. Raw source files are read from `../../../data-raw-temp/`
(never modified); processed outputs are written to `../../../data/`.

```{r set-paths}
# Trailing slash on data_dir is intentional: save_data() builds paths with paste0().
data_dir <- "../../../data/"
raw_dir  <- "../../../data-raw-temp"
```

# 2. Define target ACS variables

## 2.1 Load ACS variable dictionaries

The full ACS variable dictionaries are loaded for interactive lookup of Census
table/variable codes while selecting measures. They are not used in any
downstream transformation.

```{r load-variable-dictionaries}
v16 <- load_variables(2016, "acs5")
v24 <- load_variables(2024, "acs5")
```

## 2.2 Specify variables to extract

`tract_vars` maps short, analysis-friendly names to Census variable codes and
is shared by the 2016 and 2024 tract requests. `block_group_vars` is derived by
filtering out the aliases configured in §1.2, preserving retained names, codes,
and order. Inline comments give the plain-language meaning of each code.

This set includes vacancy-status detail from table B25004: `vac_forrent` (vacant
units for rent), `vac_rented` (rented, not occupied), and `vac_forsale` (vacant
units for sale only). No rental-inventory calculation is performed here.

### Decision: Share the full tract list and remove B25111/B25113 measures

Remove all selected B25111 measures, including its total, and both selected
B25113 measures from both survey years. Keep the three existing duplicate-code
aliases (`grent_3`, `grent_20`, `grent_26`) in the request vectors. In wide output,
tidycensus returns each distinct code under its first alias (`grentcat1`,
`grentcat18`, `grentcat24`); requested-alias counts are not output-column counts.

```{r specify-variables}
# Full tract mapping, shared by both survey years
tract_vars <- c(pop="B01003_001",      # 	TOTAL POPULATION
              pop_rent="B25008_003", # Renter Population (Total Population in Occupied Housing Units by Tenure: Total Renter-Occupied
              hu="B25001_001", # Total Housing units
              # hu_ten="B25003_001", # Total Housing Unites (by tenure)
              hh="B11001_001", # Total Households
              sfd_base="B25024_001",
              sfd_det="B25024_002", #single_family detached
              sfd_att="B25024_003", # single-family attached
              duplex="B25024_004", # 2 units
              quadplex="B25024_005", # 3 or 4 units
              mf_5_9="B25024_006", # 5 to 9 units
              mf_10_19="B25024_007", # 10 to 19 units
              mf_20_49="B25024_008", # 20 to 49 units
              mf_50="B25024_009", # 50 and over
              mobhm="B25024_010", # Mobile home
              oth_units="B25024_011", # Boat, RV, van, etc
              rhu_base= "B25003_001",
              rhu="B25003_003", # Renter Occupied Housing Units
              ohu="B25003_002", # Owner occupied Housing Units
              rent="B25064_001", # Median gross rent
              rent1bdr="B25031_003", # Median rent for 1 bedroom
              rent2bdr="B25031_004", # Median rent for 2 bedroom
              rent3bdr="B25031_005", # Median rent for 3 bedroom
              rhutot = "B25063_001", # Number of units with rent computed
              rhucash = "B25063_002",
              rhunocash = "B25063_027",
              grentcat1="B25063_003", # 	GROSS RENT-Less than $100
              grentcat2="B25063_004", # 	GROSS RENT-$100-149
              grentcat3="B25063_005", # 	GROSS RENT-$150-199
              grentcat4="B25063_006", # 	GROSS RENT-$200-249
              grentcat5="B25063_007", # 	GROSS RENT-$250-299
              grentcat6="B25063_008", # 	GROSS RENT-$300-349
              grentcat7="B25063_009", # 	GROSS RENT-$350-399
              grentcat8="B25063_010", # 	GROSS RENT-$400-449
              grentcat9="B25063_011", # 	GROSS RENT-$450-499
              grentcat10 = "B25063_012", # GROSS RENT-$500-549
              grentcat11 = "B25063_013", # GROSS RENT-$550-599
              grentcat12 = "B25063_014", # GROSS RENT-$600-649
              grentcat13 = "B25063_015", # GROSS RENT-$650-699
              grentcat14 = "B25063_016", # GROSS RENT-$700-749
              grentcat15 = "B25063_017",  # GROSS RENT-$750-799
              grentcat16 = "B25063_018", # GROSS RENT-$800-899
              grentcat17 = "B25063_019", # GROSS RENT-$900-999
              grentcat18 = "B25063_020", # GROSS RENT-$1,000-1,249
              grentcat19 = "B25063_021", # GROSS RENT-$1,250-1,499
              grentcat20 = "B25063_022", # GROSS RENT-$1,500-1,999
              grentcat21 = "B25063_023", # GROSS RENT-$2,000-2,499
              grentcat22 = "B25063_024", # GROSS RENT-$2,500-2,999
              grentcat23 = "B25063_025",  # GROSS RENT-$3,000-3,499
              grentcat24 = "B25063_026",  # GROSS RENT-$3,500 or Greater
              # pop_race="B03002_001", # Total: Hispanic or Latino by Race
              # pop_nhspwt="B03002_003", # Total: Non-Hispanic White
              # pop_nhspblk="B03002_004", # Total: Non-Hispanic Black
              # pop_hsp="B03002_012", # Total: Hispanic
              # pop_hspwt="B03002_013", # Total: Hispanic White
              # pop_hspblk="B03002_014", # Total: Hispanic Black
              med_hval = "B25077_001", # Median house value
              pop_race="B02001_001", # Total: Race
              pop_blk="B02001_003", # Black pop
              pop_aa="B02001_005", # Asian pop
              pop_ethn="B03003_001", # Total: Ethnicity pop
              pop_hsp="B03003_003", # Hispanic pop
              lqcrent="B25057_001", # LOWER CONTRACT RENT QUARTILE (DOLLARS)
              grent_3="B25063_003", # 	GROSS RENT-Less than $100
              grent_20="B25063_020", # 	GROSS RENT-$1,000 to $1,249
              grent_26="B25063_026", # 	GROSS RENT-$3,500 or more
              med_hhinc= "B19013_001", # Median Household income
              tot_vac_base= "B25002_001", # Total housing units (occupancy-status base)
              tot_vac= "B25002_003", # Vacant housing units
              vac_forrent= "B25004_002", # Vacant: for rent (available rental units)
              vac_rented= "B25004_003", # Vacant: rented, not occupied
              vac_forsale= "B25004_004" # Vacant: for sale only (available for-sale units)
              )
block_group_vars <- tract_vars[
  !names(tract_vars) %in% block_group_unavailable_vars
]

stopifnot(
  "Tract aliases must be unique" = !anyDuplicated(names(tract_vars)),
  "Block-group exclusions must be unique tract aliases" =
    !anyDuplicated(block_group_unavailable_vars) &&
    all(block_group_unavailable_vars %in% names(tract_vars)),
  "Block-group mapping must preserve retained aliases, codes, and order" =
    identical(block_group_vars,
              tract_vars[!names(tract_vars) %in% block_group_unavailable_vars]),
  "B25111/B25113 must not be requested" =
    !any(grepl("^B251(11|13)_", c(tract_vars, block_group_vars))),
  "Both rental vacancy inventory components must be retained" =
    identical(unname(tract_vars[c("vac_forrent", "vac_rented")]),
              c("B25004_002", "B25004_003")) &&
    identical(block_group_vars[c("vac_forrent", "vac_rented")],
              tract_vars[c("vac_forrent", "vac_rented")])
)

tibble(
  request = c("tract", "block group"),
  aliases = c(length(tract_vars), length(block_group_vars)),
  distinct_codes = c(n_distinct(tract_vars), n_distinct(block_group_vars))
)
```

# 3. Import and prepare 2012–2016 ACS tract data

## 3.1 Download 2016 ACS tract estimates

Pulls the selected variables for all California census tracts from the 2012–2016
ACS 5-year file in wide format (one column per estimate `*E` and margin of error
`*M`). Expected: one row per CA 2010-vintage tract (~8,057).

```{r download-acs-tract-16}
acs_trt_16 <- get_acs(geography = "tract",
                       state = "CA",
                       variables = tract_vars,
                       year = 2016,
                       output = "wide",
                       survey = "acs5")

report_n(acs_trt_16, "2016 ACS tracts imported")
acs_trt_16_n <- nrow(acs_trt_16)
```

## 3.2 Check missingness and margins of error

Quick data-quality probe on two bellwether estimates (population and median
gross rent): counts, missingness, mean/range, and mean margin of error.

```{r check-missingness-16}
vars <- c("popE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(vars, ~summ_var(acs_trt_16, .x))
out
```

## 3.3 Rename geographic ID and save

Renames `GEOID` to `tr2010_id` (and tags the table with the `rent_id` join
flag), then writes the output. **Output:** `acs_step1_2016_tract.feather` — 2012–2016 ACS
estimates with one row per 2010 CA tract, consumed by `02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd`.

```{r save-acs-tract-16}
acs_trt_16 <- download_rent_evidence(acs_trt_16, 2016)
acs_trt_16 <- rename_id(acs_trt_16, tr2010_id, GEOID)

report_n(acs_trt_16, "2016 ACS tracts saved")
save_data(acs_trt_16, data_dir, "acs_step1_2016_tract.feather")

rm(v16)
```

# 4. Import and prepare 2020–2024 ACS block-group data

## 4.1 Download 2024 ACS block-group estimates

### Decision: Use block groups for downstream geographic harmonization

The 2020–2024 ACS input for stage 2 is imported at the **block-group** level, because
2020-vintage block groups can be allocated to 2010 tracts using the NHGIS
crosswalk loaded in Section 6.1. Aggregation to 2010 tracts happens downstream in
`02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd`. The request uses the subset defined in §2.2; the full 2024
tract list is downloaded separately in §5. Expected: one row per CA 2020-vintage
block group (~25,000+).

### Decision: Validate the wide extract without rejecting missing estimates

Immediately after extraction, require one row per nonmissing, character,
12-digit BG GEOID. Required numeric estimate/MOE columns come from the first
alias of each distinct code in `block_group_vars`, so the checks track the
current request and its exclusions. Duplicate rows or columns, missing required
columns, and wrong storage types stop execution. Legitimate numeric `NA`/`NaN`
estimates remain unchanged for Step 2 completeness handling.

```{r download-acs-bg-24}
acs_bg_24 <- get_acs(geography = "block group",
                       state = "CA",
                       variables = block_group_vars,
                       year = 2024,
                       output = "wide",
                       survey = "acs5")

assert_acs_bg_input(acs_bg_24, block_group_vars, key = "GEOID", require_flag = FALSE)
report_n(acs_bg_24, "2024 ACS block groups imported")
acs_bg_24_n <- nrow(acs_bg_24)

# # Retained exploratory code: earlier pct/CV derivations, kept for reference.
# # These rely on calc_cv()/calc_pct() helpers and are computed downstream instead.

#          huCV = calc_cv(huE, huM),
#          rentCV = calc_cv(rentE, rentM),
#          pctrhu = calc_pct(rhuE, rhu_baseE),
#          pctvac = calc_pct(tot_vacE, tot_vac_baseE),
#          pctblk = calc_pct(pop_blkE, pop_raceE),
#          pctaa = calc_pct(pop_aaE, pop_raceE),
#          pcthsp = calc_pct(pop_hspE, pop_raceE),
#          pctsfd = calc_pct(sfd_detE, sfd_baseE)
#          )
```

## 4.2 Check missingness and margins of error

Same bellwether data-quality probe as Section 3.2, on the block-group data.

```{r check-missingness-bg-24}
vars <- c("popE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(vars, ~summ_var(acs_bg_24, .x))
out
```

## 4.3 Rename geographic ID and save

Renames `GEOID` to `bg2020_id` (and tags the `rent_id` flag), then writes the
output. **Output:** `acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates with one row
per 2020 CA block group, consumed by `02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd`.

```{r save-acs-bg-24}
acs_bg_24 <- download_rent_evidence(acs_bg_24, 2024, "block group")
acs_bg_24 <- rename_id(acs_bg_24, bg2020_id, GEOID)
assert_acs_bg_input(acs_bg_24, block_group_vars)
stopifnot("BG rows changed before saving" = nrow(acs_bg_24) == acs_bg_24_n)

report_n(acs_bg_24, "2024 ACS block groups saved")
save_data(acs_bg_24, data_dir, "acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather")
```

# 5. Import and prepare 2020–2024 ACS tract data

## 5.1 Download 2024 ACS tract estimates

Download the full `tract_vars` mapping, including the three bedroom-rent
measures, for all California 2020-vintage tracts. Stage 2 consumes this direct
tract input separately from the block-group input in §4. Expected: one row per
CA 2020-vintage tract, retained on `tr2020_id` in the tract-source assembly path.

```{r download-acs-tract-24}
acs_trt_24 <- get_acs(geography = "tract",
                       state = "CA",
                       variables = tract_vars,
                       year = 2024,
                       output = "wide",
                       survey = "acs5")

report_n(acs_trt_24, "2024 ACS tracts imported")
acs_trt_24_n <- nrow(acs_trt_24)
```

## 5.2 Check missingness and margins of error

Repeat the population and median-gross-rent data-quality probe on the tract data.

```{r check-missingness-tract-24}
vars <- c("popE", "rentE")

out <- map_dfr(vars, ~summ_var(acs_trt_24, .x))
out
```

## 5.3 Rename geographic ID and save

Rename `GEOID` to `tr2020_id`, preserve `NAME`, and add the logical `rent_id`
flag. **Output:** `acs_step1_2024_tract.feather` — one row per 2020 CA tract.
Keep the shared variable vectors available for final output validation.

```{r save-acs-tract-24}
acs_trt_24 <- download_rent_evidence(acs_trt_24, 2024)
acs_trt_24 <- rename_id(acs_trt_24, tr2020_id, GEOID)

report_n(acs_trt_24, "2024 ACS tracts saved")
save_data(acs_trt_24, data_dir, "acs_step1_2024_tract.feather")

rm(v24)
```

# 6. Import and prepare geographic crosswalks

## 6.1 Crosswalk 2024 block groups to 2010 tracts

### Decision: Use NHGIS weighted crosswalks for geographic harmonization

We use the NHGIS block-group-to-tract crosswalk, which provides allocation
weights (`wt_pop`, `wt_hh`, `wt_hu`, `wt_renthu`) giving the share of each source
geography's population / households / housing units / renter housing units that
falls into each target tract. Downstream aggregation (`02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd`) uses
these weights to apportion block-group estimates to 2010 tracts.

Because a single block group can split across multiple tracts (and vice versa),
the crosswalk is intentionally **many-to-many**: the unique row key is the
(`bg2020_id`, `tr2010_id`) pair, not either ID alone.

### Decision: Validate original allocation links and full-source weight sums

Read both GEOIDs explicitly as character to retain leading zeros. Require
12-digit BG and 11-digit tract IDs, unique allocation pairs, and all four
numeric weights finite and in `[0,1]`. Cross-state IDs are permitted. Before
saving, each source's weights across **all** destinations must sum to one within
the existing Step 2 tolerance of `1e-6`. Failed reconciliation stops execution;
no links or weights are changed, dropped, or renormalized. Retain the validated
`xwalk_bg_24` object for exact readback comparison in §7.6.

### Decision: Keep statewide coverage differences diagnostic

Report ACS BGs absent from the crosswalk and crosswalk BGs absent from ACS
separately, using distinct BGs rather than allocation-row counts. Summaries by
source state/county and up to ten example IDs per direction keep the display
compact. Full ID tables and unmatched crosswalk links/weights remain available
in `bg_coverage_24`. Coverage differences alone do not stop Step 1 or filter
either input; Step 2 handles contributor completeness for its target tracts.

```{r import-xwalk-bg-tr}
xwalk <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nhgis", "nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06",
                            "nhgis_bg2020_tr2010_06.csv"),
                  col_types = cols(bg2020ge = col_character(),
                                   tr2010ge = col_character())) |>
  mutate(x_id = TRUE)

report_n(xwalk, "bg2020->tr2010 crosswalk imported")
xbg_n <- nrow(xwalk)

# Rename IDs and retain the validated object through final readback.
xwalk_bg_24 <- xwalk |>
  rename(bg2020_id = bg2020ge,
         tr2010_id = tr2010ge) |>
  select(bg2020_id, tr2010_id, all_of(bg_allocation_weight_columns()), x_id)
stopifnot("Crosswalk rows changed before saving" = nrow(xwalk_bg_24) == xbg_n)
xbg_weight_sums <- assert_bg_crosswalk(xwalk_bg_24)

# Missing-data check on the weight columns
xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_pop, wt_hh), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_hu, wt_renthu), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

# Key check: rows should be unique on the (block group, tract) pair.
# Duplicate block-group IDs are EXPECTED here (split block groups).
cat(sprintf(
  "bg2020->tr2010: %s rows | %s unique (bg, tract) pairs | %s block groups | %s tracts\n",
  formatC(nrow(xwalk), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$bg2020ge, xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$bg2020ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
))

bg_coverage_24 <- bg_coverage_diagnostics(acs_bg_24, xwalk_bg_24)
cat("Statewide ACS/crosswalk coverage (diagnostic only):\n")
print(bg_coverage_24$summary, n = Inf)
print(bg_coverage_24$by_county, n = Inf)
cat("ACS-only BG examples (up to 10; all IDs in bg_coverage_24$acs_only):\n")
print(head(bg_coverage_24$acs_only, 10L))
cat("Crosswalk-only BG examples (up to 10; all IDs in bg_coverage_24$crosswalk_only):\n")
print(head(bg_coverage_24$crosswalk_only, 10L))

# Output: xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather — 2020 block group -> 2010 tract weights
report_n(xwalk_bg_24, "bg2020->tr2010 crosswalk saved")
xwalk_bg_24 |>
  arrow::write_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather"))

rm(xwalk)
```

## 6.2 Crosswalk 2000 tracts to 2010 tracts

The NHGIS 2000-tract-to-2010-tract crosswalk, used to harmonize 2000-vintage
tract geographies to 2010 tracts. As in Section 6.1 the crosswalk is
many-to-many, keyed on the (`tr2000_id`, `tr2010_id`) pair.

```{r import-xwalk-tr-tr}
xwalk <- read_csv(file.path(raw_dir, "nhgis", "nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06",
                            "nhgis_tr2000_tr2010_06.csv")) |>
  mutate(x_id = TRUE)

report_n(xwalk, "tr2000->tr2010 crosswalk imported")
xtr_n <- nrow(xwalk)

# Missing-data check on the weight columns
xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_pop, wt_hh), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

xwalk |>
  summarise(
    across(c(wt_hu, wt_renthu), list(
      n = ~sum(!is.na(.)),
      pct_missing = ~100 * sum(is.na(.)) / n(),
      mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
      min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
      max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")
  )

# Key check: rows should be unique on the (2000 tract, 2010 tract) pair.
# Duplicate 2000-tract IDs are EXPECTED here (split tracts).
cat(sprintf(
  "tr2000->tr2010: %s rows | %s unique (tr2000, tr2010) pairs | %s 2000 tracts | %s 2010 tracts\n",
  formatC(nrow(xwalk), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2000ge, xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2000ge), format = "d", big.mark = ","),
  formatC(n_distinct(xwalk$tr2010ge), format = "d", big.mark = ",")
))

# Rename to pipeline ID names and keep only key + weight columns
xwalk <- xwalk |>
  rename(tr2000_id = tr2000ge,
         tr2010_id = tr2010ge) |>
  select(c(tr2000_id, tr2010_id, wt_pop, wt_hh, wt_hu, wt_renthu, x_id))

# Output: xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather — 2000 tract -> 2010 tract weights
report_n(xwalk, "tr2000->tr2010 crosswalk saved")
xwalk |>
  arrow::write_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather"))

rm(xwalk)
```

# 7. Validate outputs

Re-load all five outputs from `../../../data/` and check required/omitted
columns, row preservation from import through save/reload, key uniqueness,
critical missingness, logical flags, and numeric distributions. These checks
run when the analyst executes the notebook. Assertions stop on contract
violations; reported estimate missingness and unusual values require review.
For the two block-group allocation inputs, §7.6 also revalidates structure and
requires exact equality with the in-memory objects validated before saving.

```{r reload-outputs}
acs16_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step1_2016_tract.feather"))
acs24_bg_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather"))
acs24_trt_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step1_2024_tract.feather"))
xbg_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather"))
xtr_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "xwalk_tr00_tr10.feather"))

output_checks <- list(
  acs_step1_2016_tract = list(
    data = acs16_out, keys = "tr2010_id", imported_n = acs_trt_16_n,
    flag = "rent_id", variables = tract_vars
  ),
  acs_step1_2024_block_group = list(
    data = acs24_bg_out, keys = "bg2020_id", imported_n = acs_bg_24_n,
    flag = "rent_id", variables = block_group_vars
  ),
  acs_step1_2024_tract = list(
    data = acs24_trt_out, keys = "tr2020_id", imported_n = acs_trt_24_n,
    flag = "rent_id", variables = tract_vars
  ),
  xwalk_bg24_tr10 = list(
    data = xbg_out, keys = c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"),
    imported_n = xbg_n, flag = "x_id"
  ),
  xwalk_tr00_tr10 = list(
    data = xtr_out, keys = c("tr2000_id", "tr2010_id"),
    imported_n = xtr_n, flag = "x_id"
  )
)
```

## 7.1 Check required and omitted columns

Each ACS output must contain `NAME`, its geographic key, estimate/MOE pairs
for the distinct requested codes and `rent_id`. The three duplicate-code aliases remain configured, but the first
alias per code determines the required returned columns. Both tract outputs
must include all three bedroom-rent pairs; the block-group output must omit
them. No output may contain the seven removed B25111/B25113 measure pairs
or the retired low-rent counts.
Crosswalks must retain both keys, all four weights, and `x_id`.

```{r validate-columns}
removed_measures <- c(
  "rentyrblt", "rentyrblt_14_16", "rentyrblt_10_13",
  "rentyrblt_00_09", "rentyrblt_90_99", "rentmv1yr", "rentmv5yr"
)
weight_columns <- bg_allocation_weight_columns()

for (output_name in names(output_checks)) {
  check <- output_checks[[output_name]]
  df <- check$data
  if (!is.null(check$variables)) {
    numeric_columns <- acs_request_columns(check$variables)
    required <- c(check$keys, "NAME", numeric_columns, check$flag)
    omitted_aliases <- c(removed_measures,
                        setdiff(names(tract_vars), names(check$variables)))
    omitted <- c(as.vector(outer(omitted_aliases, c("E", "M"), paste0)),
                 grep("^B251(11|13)_", names(df), value = TRUE), "rhu_lrE", "rhu_lr2E")
  } else {
    numeric_columns <- weight_columns
    required <- c(check$keys, numeric_columns, check$flag)
    omitted <- character()
  }
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required, names(df))
  omitted_present <- intersect(omitted, names(df))
  cat(output_name, "| missing required:", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "),
      "| excluded columns present:", paste(omitted_present, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  stopifnot(
    "Required columns missing" = length(missing_columns) == 0L,
    "Excluded columns present" = length(omitted_present) == 0L,
    "Duplicate column names" = !anyDuplicated(names(df)),
    "Keys must be character" = all(vapply(df[check$keys], is.character, logical(1))),
    "Measures/weights must be numeric" =
      all(vapply(df[numeric_columns], is.numeric, logical(1)))
  )
  if (!is.null(check$variables)) {
    stopifnot("NAME must be character" = is.character(df$NAME))
  }
}
```

## 7.2 Check row preservation and key uniqueness

Expected: each saved output retains exactly its imported row count. The ACS
tables are unique on their geographic ID; crosswalks are unique on their
(source, target) key pair, with individual source/target IDs repeating by design.

```{r validate-keys}
for (output_name in names(output_checks)) {
  check <- output_checks[[output_name]]
  duplicate_n <- sum(duplicated(check$data[check$keys]))
  cat(output_name, "| imported:", check$imported_n,
      "| reloaded:", nrow(check$data), "| duplicate keys:", duplicate_n, "\n")
  stopifnot(
    "Rows changed between import and reload" = nrow(check$data) == check$imported_n,
    "Empty output" = nrow(check$data) > 0L,
    "Duplicate geographic keys" = duplicate_n == 0L
  )
}
```

## 7.3 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing or blank geographic IDs. Some missingness in ACS estimates,
including median rent for sparsely-renter-occupied geographies, is expected;
report counts without imposing an empirical threshold. Crosswalk weights must
be finite and in [0, 1].

```{r validate-missingness}
for (output_name in names(output_checks)) {
  check <- output_checks[[output_name]]
  df <- check$data
  stopifnot("Missing or blank geographic keys" =
              all(vapply(df[check$keys], function(x) !anyNA(x) && all(nzchar(x)),
                         logical(1))))
  critical <- if (!is.null(check$variables)) {
    # c(check$keys, "NAME", "popE", "rentE", "rhuE", "rhu_baseE", "vac_forrentE", "vac_rentedE",
    #   intersect(paste0(block_group_unavailable_vars, "E"), names(df)))
    c(
      check$keys,
      "NAME",
      "popE",
      "med_hhincE",
      "rentE",
      "rhuE",
      "rhu_baseE",
      "vac_forrentE",
      "vac_rentedE",

      paste0("grentcat", 1:24, "E"),

      "sfd_baseE",
      "sfd_detE",
      "sfd_attE",
      "duplexE",
      "quadplexE",
      "mf_5_9E",
      "mf_10_19E",
      "mf_20_49E",
      "mf_50E",

      intersect(
        paste0(block_group_unavailable_vars, "E"),
        names(df)
      )
    )
  } else {
    c(check$keys, weight_columns)
  }
  cat(output_name, "| missing values by critical column:\n")
  print(colSums(is.na(df[critical])))
  if (is.null(check$variables)) {
    stopifnot("Invalid crosswalk weights" =
                all(vapply(df[weight_columns], function(x) {
                  all(is.finite(x) & x >= 0 & x <= 1)
                }, logical(1))))
  }
}
```

## 7.4 Check flag-variable encoding

The join flags (`rent_id`, `x_id`) must be logical, non-missing, and constant
`TRUE` for these source tables.

```{r validate-flags}
for (output_name in names(output_checks)) {
  check <- output_checks[[output_name]]
  flag <- check$data[[check$flag]]
  cat(output_name, check$flag, "| class:", class(flag),
      "| values:", paste(unique(flag), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  stopifnot("Invalid source join flag" = is.logical(flag) && !anyNA(flag) && all(flag))
}
```

## 7.5 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in each output. Review negative
estimates/MOEs, non-finite values other than `NA`, and ranges implausible for ACS
counts or dollar measures. Estimate missingness is reported separately in §7.3.

```{r validate-numeric-summaries}
for (output_name in names(output_checks)) {
  df <- output_checks[[output_name]]$data
  print_numeric_summary(df, output_name)
  numeric_columns <- names(df)[vapply(df, is.numeric, logical(1))]
  unusual <- vapply(df[numeric_columns], function(x) {
    sum(!is.na(x) & (!is.finite(x) | x < 0))
  }, numeric(1))
  if (any(unusual > 0)) {
    cat("REVIEW:", output_name, "has negative or non-finite numeric values:\n")
    print(unusual[unusual > 0])
  }
}
```

## 7.6 Verify exact block-group and crosswalk readback

Both inputs must retain the validated row count, geographic keys and row order,
column names/order, storage types/classes, and every value (including missing
estimates). Every crosswalk weight must match exactly after Feather reload;
the `1e-6` source-sum tolerance does **not** permit serialization differences.
Recheck BG structure and full-source weight reconciliation on the reloaded data.

```{r validate-bg-readback}
assert_step1_readback(acs24_bg_out, acs_bg_24, "bg2020_id", "2024 ACS block groups")
assert_step1_readback(xbg_out, xwalk_bg_24, c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"),
                      "BG-to-2010-tract crosswalk")
assert_acs_bg_input(acs24_bg_out, block_group_vars)
xbg_reloaded_weight_sums <- assert_bg_crosswalk(xbg_out)
```
